claims.text: Uncoated tungsten particles exhibit poor interfacial wetting with copper, leading to voids and imperfect bonding.
Tungsten particles will be coated with a uniform 100–200 nm electroless Ni or Cu–Ni layer before blending with copper powder.
The coated W–Cu powder will be spark-plasma sintered at approximately 900–950 °C and 50–100 MPa under vacuum or inert atmosphere.
A low-temperature pre-sintering stage will restrict excessive diffusion and intermetallic-phase growth.
A continuous nanoscale Ni-rich interlayer acts as a diffusion bridge between tungsten and copper.
The Ni-rich interlayer enhances wetting between tungsten and copper.
The Ni-rich interlayer promotes filling of interfacial voids during sintering.
The Ni coating reduces the interfacial-energy barrier between tungsten and copper.
The Ni coating facilitates solid-state diffusion during spark-plasma sintering.
Controlled interdiffusion promotes metallurgical bonding at W–Cu interfaces.
Controlled interdiffusion minimizes gas entrapment and interfacial void formation.
Ni-coated samples will have near-perfect interfacial bonding and significantly lower porosity than W–Cu composites made by SPS with uncoated tungsten.
Ni-coated samples will exhibit higher thermal conductivity than the uncoated-SPS baseline.
Ni-coated samples will exhibit greater mechanical durability under irradiation than the uncoated-SPS baseline.
Processing will be maintained below the melting point of copper while remaining sufficiently hot for solid-state diffusion.
The intended service environment is a high-temperature, irradiation-exposed fusion-reactor joint.
Excessive W–Ni–Cu intermetallic formation could compromise high-temperature performance.

The hypothesis will be falsified if coated samples fail to show statistically significant improvements in bonding, porosity, thermal properties, and mechanical properties relative to the control, or if brittle intermetallics impair performance.

contradictions.description: The named baseline is conventional SPS of uncoated tungsten, but the experimental control also receives the added low-temperature pre-sintering stage. Unless that stage is part of the conventional baseline, the tested control does not exactly match the stated baseline.
